Learn the source sequence in [shared Xmon inputs](tutorial-xmon-input.qmd) and
[source observations](course/source-observations.qmd). The [geometry concept](concepts/geometry.qmd) explains the identities; this page owns their exact contract.

The in-tree `scgsim.sgb` package is SCGSim's current geometry and topology
authority. It consumes structured PDK and component semantics and must not
reconstruct geometry meaning from solver-generated labels.

`build_component_stack()` composes two explicit authorities. PDK
`LayerStack` records supply materials, process layers, Z/thickness,
conductor/solution roles, and exact host volumes. Component annotations supply
local entity identity, ports, functional conductor regions, and topology
selectors. The Notebook composes named occurrences and assigns the final net
map; it does not author PDK or component facts manually.

In the public Xmon composition, the reusable child keeps its local pad,
coupler, mask, and a ground-arm metal contribution. That arm overlaps the
residual ground plane, so it is not a separate conductor Entity; modeling it
as one would duplicate metal. The root composition supplies one D0 and one D1
plane through the existing stack recipe, then unions the occurrence-local arm
geometry into the D1 plane using an explicit physical conductor-layer
binding; the draw or mask layer does not imply that target. It does not copy
full ground-plane Entities into each child occurrence or create planes
automatically. The Notebook owns the final `Net -> Entity` map across the
common planes, local device Entities, and named ground connections. Geometry
does not infer electrical connectivity or merge child net maps.

## Component-to-backend geometry contract

The current candidate makes local component geometry and hierarchy explicit
before Palace or AEDT preparation. The public `scgsim.sgb.GeometryPlan` is the
mutable Notebook builder: it inventories expanded component entities and
stores the final `Net -> Entity` assignment. Its `prepare()` method returns an
immutable `GeometryPlanSnapshot`; `GeometryBuildInput` remains the normalized
geometry boundary consumed by the backend preparation paths.

Create the plan with `GeometryPlan(component=assembled, root_id="chip",
layer_stack=..., material_records=..., coupon_padding_um=...)`. Register each
named reference occurrence in parent-first order with
`register_instance("chip/q0", q0_ref)`. `plan.entities` exposes the existing
semantic entity inventory with slash-qualified `.semantic_id` values. The
Notebook supplies the final map with
`set_nets({NetID: tuple(qualified_entity_ids)})`; `prepare()` returns a frozen
`GeometryPlanSnapshot` containing the normalized `geometry_input`, stack, GDS
bytes and digest, and detached source-occurrence records. It retains no live
component references. Palace and AEDT consume that exact snapshot through
`EigenmodeSim.set_plan(snapshot)`.

For component-semantics schema v2, the paired stack adds derived source
occurrence records, not a new user polygon-selection API. Each
`metadata.source_occurrences` row binds a registered path and parent path to a
cell name, composed transform, and `reference_index`: the zero-based reference
ordinal in that parent, or `null` for the root. One registered occurrence names
one actual GDS reference. Consumers must first expand arrays into explicit
individual references; `GeometryPlan` does not auto-expand arrays. Each layer's
`geometry.source_occurrence_polygons_um` and each
`metadata.port_sheet_source_layers` entry's `source_occurrence_polygon_um`
preserve selected exterior and hole loops in micrometres. The reader checks
the paired GDS hash, binds each path to its recorded parent reference and child
cell, converts the source database units, reapplies the composed transform,
and recomputes those loops. This keeps touching same-layer geometry from
separate named occurrences distinct. Existing schema-v1 stack readers keep
their selector decoding behavior.

Component-semantics v2 also accepts
`component_semantics.ground_plane_contributions`. Each record has exactly
`local_id`, `plane_id`, `level`, `layer`, and `selector_point_um`. The local ID
names a component-local metal contribution; `plane_id` names a root-local
derived plane. `level` is the physical conductor level and must match the
target plane's `metadata.logical_layer_id`; `layer` is the source GDS
layer/datatype pair used with the local selector point. Thus a draw or mask
layer does not implicitly choose the target conductor face.

Preparation uses the selector to resolve one connected occurrence-local metal
region on the declared source GDS layer. That region can contain multiple
fused raw GDS polygons. GeometryPlan applies the occurrence transform once,
verifies the resulting exterior and hole loops against the paired GDS, and
records them in the root plane's `geometry.source_occurrence_includes`. The
root plane's `metadata.ground_plane_contribution_sources` retains the
occurrence path, local ID, physical level, and source layer. A selected region
that contains a separately declared local conductor on the same physical level
is rejected. These includes become part of the residual plane before polygon
lowering; they are not separate conductor Entities or Net assignments, and
GeometryPlan does not infer connectivity or promise separate measurements.

The plan owns the shared outer vacuum envelope. Set it before `prepare()` with
`plan.set_vacuum_region(padding=...)`, using the existing scalar, X/Y/Z tuple,
or six-face micrometre mapping forms. Both backends receive that same envelope;
once a `Sim` consumes a plan snapshot, attempts to add standalone
`set_geometry()` or `set_stack()` input, or a conflicting Palace
`set_vacuum_region()` / `set_airbox()` value, fail atomically. They cannot
replace only part of the bound source. To change the component, stack, or
boundary, update the plan and prepare a new snapshot, then call `set_plan()`
with it. A legacy standalone-input workflow uses a fresh `Sim`. No default
padding is inferred. Authored `D0_TO_D1_GAP` remains a separate vacuum entity
inside the outer region.

Component annotation schema v2 keeps conductor-region identity, level, layer,
and topology selector local to the component; it removes component-level net
and group assignments. Optional port records identify the local source layer
and target logical layer. Plan preparation verifies each source port and its
sheet and transforms the sheet once. Qualified lineage then identifies, for
example, `chip/q0/o_junction_lumped`. Palace binds that qualified port name to
its target logical layer; an AEDT junction uses the same normalized source
sheet and its recorded overlaps.

| Fact or operation | Candidate contract |
|---|---|
| Component definition | Holds local polygons, source Entity IDs, ports, topology selectors, and local component facts. Reusing a component does not rewrite its local IDs. Schema v2 does not assign final Nets or expose a public `Group` API inside the component. |
| Component occurrence | `register_instance(path, reference)` binds a named path to the actual GDSFactory occurrence. Parent segments are registered before children. The path scopes entity and polygon identities before flattening; rotation and reflection apply consistently to geometry, selectors, and ports. |
| Notebook net mapping | Authors only the final `Net -> Entity` map on the `GeometryPlan`; components do not carry intermediate or child net assignments. Membership may be assigned once to one net; duplicate membership on the same net is deduplicated. There is no public component `Group` API, implicit connectivity, or child-net merge framework. |
| Assignment validation | Mapping updates are atomic. Unknown or ambiguous entity references and an entity assigned across different nets reject the whole update. An unmapped entity remains unassigned (`None`); a backend requires a net binding only where that backend operation needs one. |
| Source lineage | The immutable snapshot preserves source Entity and polygon identities separately from derived group membership. An Entity is lineage, not a promise of a raw per-Entity measurement or field expression. A `semantic_group_id` is not reused as Entity identity or source lineage. |
| Computational groups | New physical mesh grouping serves high-count geometry only. Copies may share one computational physical group when explicit Net, material, local source Entity ID, parent occurrence context, and role all match. Qualified Entity/member lineage remains available; an unassigned Net stays separate. For example, the eight sibling Ground bumps in this coupon map to one physical group while retaining eight Entity IDs. Legacy recorded physical-group policy remains version-specific. AEDT owner/interface/integral groups remain backend-specific and keep their existing policy. |
| Backend lowering | Palace and AEDT consume the same prepared source snapshot through their existing preparation paths. Native aggregates retain their source members and coverage. This does not promise per-patch native results, per-Entity raw measurements, or per-Entity field expressions. |
| Vacuum geometry | Authored vacuum entities keep their names, materials, hosts, and per-domain analysis identity. At the source-input level, the plan adds one outer background domain as the semantic complement of modeled bodies and custom regions under the established SGB priority/cut rules. The backend owns how it represents that partition natively. The public `D0_TO_D1_GAP` remains a distinct vacuum entity. |
| AEDT object names | New native names are readable and deterministic, sanitized and disambiguated as needed, and remain bound to the original qualified Entity ID. Historical prepared names keep their version-specific reader policy. |
| Boundary defaults | Palace leaves an unspecified external vacuum boundary at its natural PMC condition. AEDT uses HFSS's default Perfect E. The shared input does not convert one policy into the other. |

These are the current CONVERGING semantics. Source preparation establishes
the geometry input contract; it does not imply native geometry validation or
solver execution.

## Current Surface-EPR direction

| Route | Public intent | Current state |
|---|---|---|
| Route A | Zero-thickness face-metal PEC sheets with finite bump shells | Implemented, converging |
| Route B | The closed exterior boundary shell of a finite construction metal volume is PEC; its interior is excluded from Palace solution domains and receives no tetrahedra | Implemented, converging |

Only Route A and Route B are in the current direction.

## Internal semantic projection

SGB projects already-validated source facts once per source/model revision into
`scgsim.semantics`. The immutable projection is reused while planning a model;
it is not rebuilt by deep-copying a full stack for every interface pair.
Interface classification and each owner projection remain distinct operations:
solution solid/vacuum ordering is not interchangeable with declared surface
owners, legacy two-owner records, sheet owners, or aggregate physical-group
owners.

The projection can express finite PEC, surface-sheet MA/MS, local MM/MA patch
evidence, explicit side meaning, and outer/hole/seam provenance without
claiming that classification proves contact. Declared, planned, and observed
records remain distinguishable. Native tags and groups are opaque observations,
not reconstructed successes, and duplicate observations do not multiply one
semantic contribution.

`plan_route_surfaces()` owns the public projection boundary: it creates the
facade once when omitted, or verifies a supplied facade against the same route
and build-input fingerprint, then reuses it at the existing adjacency call
sites. Explicit authored interface kind and owner metadata take precedence
over derived defaults. Route-A sheet contact footprints remain an `MM`
topology relation but lower as the existing `MS` cap with its established
physical-name prefix; the surrounding sheet may still carry its independently
classified MA/MS evidence.

Route-A profile selection is optional for a direct semantic-core consumer.
Existing explicit Palace Route-A entry points still require
`substrate_face` or `metal_gap_equivalent`, and Route B still rejects either
profile. With no core profile, coordinates remain unchanged and no collapse is
recorded. `metal_gap_equivalent` remains the existing effective coordinate
normalization; no reversible-collapse claim is made.

For a stack with no PDK vacuum layer, omitted conductor host declarations are
bound to the internally generated background only when the caller selects
`set_vacuum_region()`. The same normalized polygon-versus-substrate-region
contact check supplies Route-A physical support for both authored-host and
generated-background stacks. It considers complete exteriors and holes and
requires a unique positive-area contact; a bounding-box intersection,
point/edge touch, or auto-region edge is insufficient. An authored
but unresolved host name still fails instead of being silently rebound.
Single-substrate `substrate_face` has no opposing die or gap value; two
opposed substrates keep physical `substrate_face` and the distinct
two-face-only `metal_gap_equivalent` normalization. The generated Region is
profiled after the source geometry and partitioned around actual dielectric
and finite-PEC occupancy. Route-A sheets do not subtract a fictitious volume.

Route-A support is local rather than a whole-sheet label. The sheet polygon is
partitioned by exact bottom/top solution coverage before bare SA/AA surfaces
are constructed, so substrate holes remain holes and a partly supported stress
case retains separate supported and exposed children. Each child keeps ordered
bottom/top evidence; an MM contact cap retains only the side left after the
contact cut. Port footprints select the intersecting child and fail if they
cross incompatible local domain pairs. Fully freestanding sheets remain
unsupported.

The same local-domain partition is used when conductor faces are removed from
an SA patch. The planner subtracts only the face overlap with that exact
solution-pair patch, even when one conductor spans several adjacent domains.
After AEDT junction partitioning, only adapter-generated Route-A sheet
footprints are rebuilt from the final conductor polygons; caller-authored
interface declarations remain intact.

Route B keeps finite geometry and records local top, bottom, and sidewall
material-side evidence. Geometry adjacency remains a set, whereas the additive
contribution ledger preserves semantic multiplicity. Two same-kind MA sides
on one Route-A child share one native surface and one aggregate Palace row;
they are not duplicated or multiplied. That aggregate requires Palace's
internal-boundary cracking and does not imply side-resolved numeric output.
The AEDT contribution catalogue is sourced from physically planned ledger
entries and groups one catalogue row by contribution identity while retaining
each distinct patch binding. A generic declaration without physical ledger
evidence remains semantic metadata and does not create an additional numeric
EPR contribution.

## Identity requirements

A handoff preserves:

- source SGB revision;
- semantic surface and volume identities;
- route choice and topology receipt;
- generated mesh/config identity;
- the mapping from solver entities back to semantic geometry.

External SGB revisions remain derivation history only. The in-tree
`scgsim.sgb` package is the current authority; no direct external consumer or
fallback path is implied.

## Shared source facts for AEDT

`GeometryPlan` is the shared source frontend for Palace and AEDT. Its prepared
snapshot includes the normalized `GeometryBuildInput` polygons (including
hole loops), entities, solution regions, source provenance, and route profile,
along with the prepared stack and source-occurrence records. Source-linked
junction declarations retain their terminal nets, direction, dimensions,
inductance, and capacitance; those fields are not retroactively attributed to
the normalized `GeometryBuildInput`. AEDT does not consume
`ConstructionPlanRecord`, Gmsh surfaces, physical groups, or native tags.

An AEDT-owned binding sidecar must separately record each created body, sheet,
face, material side, selection, and saved-field expression against those
source identities. A native face overlap or adjacency query is observed
geometry evidence; it cannot manufacture source contact intent. Route-A
profile normalization still happens once at the shared frontend boundary, and
Route-B finite-body facts stay distinct from PEC approximation and the AEDT
implementation that realizes them.

## Pre-solve input summary

`scgsim.sgb.summarize_geometry_input(build_input, *, prepared_stack)` returns an
`InputSummary` with detached `.data` and an HTML representation for notebook
display. Both Eigenmode facades expose `input_summary()` to combine this
normalized source with their configured backend settings. AEDT summarizes its
normalized build input and stack; Palace requires its bound `GeometryPlan`.
Passing a raw component without explicit normalization fails rather than
guessing a stack. The summary records source, entity, Net, material, Z/vacuum,
port, EPR, and run-control inputs; unset or unknown values stay explicit. It
does no file I/O, meshing, catalogue rebuild, or native solver inspection and
does not claim native geometry or run evidence.
For the source summary, `source.top_cell_name` uses a valid adapter-selected
`selected_cell_name` first, then falls back to legacy `top_cell_name` when the
selected name is unavailable, and otherwise is `None`. This display choice
does not mutate source metadata or reread the GDS.

Its notebook HTML presents source, backend, route, and count cards, followed by
Entity/occurrence/Net/material/source-Z, port/host/direction, junction A/B/L/C,
analysis-choice, film/loss/source/margin-assumption, and solver/resource
tables. The original detached JSON is in a collapsed disclosure. Unknown
values remain distinct from zero; `None` means all and an empty tuple means
none only for a selection, while an absent request is labeled not requested.
The HTML has no theme
argument and inherits the front-end light/dark palette; the detached `.data`
contract is unchanged.
